statement: In a promotion argument, report how many defects each review found, not how many reviews ran. A rate that is not falling toward zero argues against promoting. On 2026-10-19 I wrote a ruling on cejel#526 recommending that witan-rubric-v27 become the default. As evidence it said v27 had survived two independent adversarial reviews and that the second found no rise. A day later a third review of the merged code found eight real defects. They include a path by which A1 could stop being scored under v27, letting the composite rise, and a 12 s stall on the default rubric. The three reviews reproduced 10, 8 and 8 defects. Fix: the ruling on #526 is corrected to cite those counts and makes another clean review a precondition for any default change.
